key_insight: Subquadratic sequence models can significantly reduce the computational burden of transformers while still handling complex long-range dependencies. This paper compares xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet to identify which design choices make these efficient architectures most effective for demanding code-related tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high compute and memory cost of transformer attention, especially for long sequences and code modeling, and asks which subquadratic architecture design is most effective in practice.
method: Compare three leading subquadratic architectures: xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet.
Evaluate them on challenging dependency-heavy tasks, including code-model pre-training and distillation from large language models.
Analyze which architectural principles best balance efficiency and modeling performance for sequence learning.
impact: This helps practitioners choose efficient alternatives to transformers without guessing which subquadratic design will work best. It is especially relevant for large-scale code and sequence models where speed, scalability, and long-context reasoning matter.

paper_title: On Subquadratic Architectures: From Applications to Principles
paper_authors: Anamaria-Roberta Hartl, Levente Zólyomi, David Stap, Pieter-Jan Hoedt, Niklas Schmidinger
